snip.s: Psychiatry Year 6 CAT: October 2023, violence, defence mechanisms, hallucination

snip.t: Subdural haematoma: blood between dura and arachnoid; commonly due to torn bridging veins.
| Acute subdural haematoma | Head trauma, rapid decline, unilateral pupil dilation | CT shows crescent‑shaped bleed; often focal mass effect |
| Over-drainage | Low-pressure headache, subdural haematoma or hygroma, slit ventricle syndrome. |
snip.s: Hydrocephalus: Causes, Presentation and CSF Diversion (Shunts)

snip.t: Acute subdural haematoma: craniotomy and evacuation if thick (over 10 mm), midline shift (over 5 mm) or GCS falling.
snip.s: Head Injury: Assessment, Intracranial Haematomas and Management of Raised ICP

snip.t: Chronic subdural haematoma: burr hole drainage (two burr holes, irrigation with saline, with or without a drain).
snip.s: Head Injury: Assessment, Intracranial Haematomas and Management of Raised ICP
